title: [TRACK] Holy reliability, continuity, and cross-session roadmap
description:
Master tracker for the complete Holy session-reliability program captured from the July 2026 investigation and product discussion.

Governing invariants:
- Never guess a tmux or provider session identity.
- Unknown state is unsafe.
- Harness hooks and process facts are authoritative; screen text is only a hint.
- Restore resumes the exact conversation, is idempotent, and is manually initiated from automatically captured metadata.
- Claude, Codex, OpenCode, and future harnesses use an open adapter contract.
- No prompt, response, transcript, secret, or environment content enters metadata by default.
- Installed-app acceptance, not commit existence, closes user-visible bugs.

Wave 1 - stop active data loss and establish truth:
- mn-495322 exact tmux kill and Cocoa 3584
- mn-56f896 notes/pins/title/identity durability
- mn-ca1805 database growth verification
- mn-e13961 open harness hook/identity/model protocol
- mn-c3b48a byte-exact PTY transport

Wave 2 - accept user-visible reliability:
- mn-569b91 orphan reconciliation/reaping
- mn-8179b6 six-state indicators and notifications
- mn-679893 truthful live model display
- mn-15ba3d sync contract
- mn-9eb075 Sync Session Config UX

Wave 3 - reboot continuity:
- mn-3cdfa0 automatic recovery manifest
- mn-84c0eb exact idempotent restore engine
- mn-9a6145 Restore All/Selected and backup browser
- mn-3cd266 urgent July 15 32-session salvage

Wave 4 - cross-session eyes, then hands:
- mn-e59548 read-only holyctl list/observe
- mn-c674c4 Watch with provenance
- mn-e49b22 safe-input oracle
- mn-573ec9 brokered leases/preemption/coord/audit
- mn-610814 runtime-safe verified messages and controls

Tracking durability:
- mn-9febbc make the Manna board itself durable across computers
- Existing optional mn-211310 drag-to-reorder remains blocked by metadata durability and should be re-triaged afterward.

title: [P0][TMUX] Kill and verify the exact discovered live session

title: [P1][DB] session_events retention: unbounded growth (409 of 443 MB, ~11 MB/day); snapshot dedup verified fixed
description:
RETARGETED 2026-08-07 (Erik, /board audit decision). The original incident is solved and verified live: git_snapshots = 104 rows in the installed 443 MB DB (was 31.5M rows / ~50 GB); an unchanged poll inserts zero rows (value-compare at HolyWorkspaceDatabasePersistence.swift:583, captured_at excluded from the compared value). That half is accepted.

THE LIVE PROBLEM: session_events has no retention path at all. Measured 2026-08-07 on the installed DB: 126,497 rows / ~409 MB plus ~21 MB indexes, growing ~2,900 rows (~11 MB) per day over 39 days; 115,495 of those rows are session_runtime_updated. The only DELETE FROM statements in macos/Sources cover app_state, git_snapshots, launch_profiles, remote_hosts, sessions, tasks, templates — never session_events (rows die only by FK cascade; 0 of 265 sessions pending purge). Retention is save-triggered, so an abandoned DB never drains (debug-bundle DB: 1,036,662 git_snapshots rows / 1.33 GB, untouched since 07-13).

Done when:
- session_events carries an explicit bounded retention policy (age and/or per-session cap), drained in bounded batches without blocking foreground writes.
- Prune preserves recovery-owned metadata: protectedArchiveIDs (HolyWorkspaceRetentionPolicy.swift:24-33) currently protects only tmux-discovery-evidenced rows, so a dead crash-restore archive drops recoveryReason/recoveryBootBatchID with it — same gap as mn-569b91 criterion 5; a test must pin it.
- The validating maintenance path is wired or deleted: HolyDatabaseMaintenance (integrity_check, foreign_key_check, per-table row equality) has zero production callers; the wired compactor validates page accounting only, and launch compaction runs synchronously on the main thread (AppDelegate.swift:226).
- A production-shaped soak shows a flat growth curve on the installed database.

--- original text below for provenance ---
Original incident: git_snapshots reached 31.5M live rows and roughly 50 GB. Commits dd1b7f955 and 1f73f70ae add dedup/retention and gated compaction; treat them as evidence, not automatic acceptance.

Done when:
- An unchanged git poll inserts zero rows and a meaningful change inserts exactly one.
- Bounded maintenance drains legacy rows without blocking foreground writes.
- Archive/session retention preserves user-visible recovery metadata.
- Compaction checks free disk, is deliberate/gated, and validates sessions/events before and after.
- A production-shaped soak demonstrates a flat growth curve and the installed database remains bounded.

title: [P0][PTY] Make paste and injected input byte-exact
description:
Known open bug: large cross-session paste loses/truncates chunks and can interleave terminal UI text. Local 64-byte pacing is not proof; the drop point remains unknown.

Scope and done criteria:
- Build deterministic local, tmux, and SSH reproductions with large multiline, Unicode, and bracketed-paste payloads.
- Instrument app buffer -> PTY -> tmux -> SSH -> receiver with byte counts and checksums.
- Identify the exact loss/interleaving layer before choosing flow control, writable-drain, or tmux load/paste-buffer transport.
- Verify bracketed paste end to end.
- Delivery is checksum-exact, retryable, and fails visibly rather than silently corrupting input.

This is a hard blocker for agent-to-agent writing and autonomous control.

title: [P0][HOOKS] Complete the open harness identity, lifecycle, and model protocol

- Exact provider identity is durably persisted, not left only in memory or tmux.

title: [ACCEPT][STATE] Prove six-state indicators and reliable notifications
description:
Canonical product vocabulary from .handoff/INDICATORS-FIRST-PRINCIPLES-2026-07-14.md:
- spinner = working
- question mark = genuinely needs the user, including approval
- white dot = unread finished work
- blue dot = seen/used today
- muted grey dot = inactive 24-48 hours
- sleeping Z plus grey = inactive 48+ hours
The hand and grey checkmark are banned; unread replaces recency.

Commit 537c0a567 is implementation evidence. Done when Tier-3 screen text cannot create an operational state, unread appears within 2 seconds of committed finish, notification tokens dedupe across restart/reconnect, missed events replay exactly once, every alert has auditable evidence, and a 24-hour installed-app soak with dev servers has zero sustained false spinners.

description:

SCOPE 2026-08-07 (Erik, /board audit decision): Recovery Backups UI is split out to mn-6f00cd and is no longer part of this issue's close. This issue closes on the reopen's D1-D4 acceptance plus Erik's five-second human test. Audit 2026-08-07 verified D1-D4 fixed in code: D1 boot-batch scoping via crashRestoreBatch (HolyWorkspaceStore.swift:1682) + coldBootBatchID stamp (HolySessionSupervisor.swift:184,200); D2 selection law — freshPreselectionLimit=12, older rows unselected, Select All/None scoped to visible rows (HolyRestoreEngine.swift:323-332, HolyRestoreSheet.swift:334,340); D3 View menu 'Restore Sessions…' with real validation (MainMenu.xib:335, HolyWorkspaceWindowController.swift:242,321-329) plus the banner gated to fresh parents only; D4 Session History purpose line, crash-restore callout, per-row 'Open Session Restore' (HolySessionHistorySheet.swift:108,121-155,266). 22 new tests across batch-scoping / selection-law / signage.

Fix acceptance (human-flow, not code-flow): after a crash launch, restore reachable in one click from BOTH the banner and a durable menu item; the sheet opens scoped to the latest boot batch with older interruptions collapsed and unselected; Select All/None exist; a fresh human finds it in under five seconds.

Allow an agent or human in one project session to observe another session read-only before any control path exists.

The roster indicator heuristic is not a safety oracle. Build a narrower fail-closed gate before any peer agent may type.

Terminal prose and the user's draft can never establish readiness. Unknown means unsafe. title: [P2][CONTROL] Add brokered leases, human preemption, quotas, and audit

Implement Holy as the broker; never grant direct peer-to-pane control.

Done when there is one controller lease per target, immediate human preemption, expiry, action quotas/rate limits, permission scoping, and complete session_events audit. Integrate with or explicitly respect agent-do coord claims/focus so there are not two mutually blind ownership systems. Expired, preempted, over-quota, busy, or unknown controllers cannot send input.

title: [P2][CONTROL] Add byte-verified messages and runtime-safe control adapters

Add controlled interaction only after the broker and transport gates pass.

Done when every injected message carries mandatory disclosure such as [from claude @ session-X], provenance is visible in the target and Watch feed, delivery is paced/checksummed and acknowledged byte-for-byte, and success means an authoritative target transition rather than "the screen changed." title: [P0][STATE] Restore stalled/looping agent alerts via working-lease expiry
description:
xhigh review finding (CONFIRMED, HolySessionSupervisor.swift:1453): the screen-derived 'may be stalled/looping' notifications were deleted and the wire contract (working|needs-user|finished|failed|idle|ended) has no stalled lifecycle — a wedged agent that never emits finished/needs-user is now silent and decays to age dots while burning budget. Design: the working-claim lease expiry (envelope timestamps already bound working claims) should raise an 'agent may be stalled' alert through HolyAgentNotificationPolicy with auditable evidence. This is a hole in mn-8179b6's own acceptance ('every alert has auditable evidence' — a wedged agent produces no alert at all).

P0 2026-08-07 (Erik, /board audit decision): mn-8cec74's lease-extension work made this strictly worse — a wedged agent whose TUI keeps redrawing satisfies producerProcessAlive + fresh producerLastOutputAt and extends the working claim indefinitely (HolyModels.swift:421-441); the 30-minute cutoff no longer bites for exactly the wedged-agent case this issue exists to catch. Note also producerLastOutputAt is window-scoped (tmux window_activity), so a chatty neighbor pane in the same window can hold a dead claim alive.

title: [P2][UX][HOOKS] Remote bridge installer should recognize a host's own local Holy installation
description: Observed 2026-07-15: MacBook Hosts sheet reports the Studio's authoritative-indicator bridge as blocked ('a guarded user setting already has a different value') — but the Studio has a complete, healthy, Holy-owned v3 LOCAL install. Root cause: local installs write notify as ~/Library/Application Support/Holy Ghostty/holy-codex-turn-complete.py while remote installs use ~/.local/share/holy-ghostty/; same guarded key (codex top-level notify), different Holy-owned value, so the remote guarded-merge fails closed (correct — otherwise two Holy apps would flip-flop the line). Fix: when the existing guarded line carries Holy's ownership marker with the LOCAL path convention, report the host as 'locally managed by Holy Ghostty on that host' (informational, not blocked) and skip remote management for that harness. Never let two installers co-manage one guarded key. Ref: HolyAgentStateBridge.swift guardedTextDocuments (~:248), HolyRemoteAgentStateBridgeService.swift foreign-guarded-setting (~:565).

title: [P0][STATE] True recency: blue keys to HUMAN use (user-prompt events + focus dwell); violet 'on automation'; green pip unread
description:
REFINED by Erik 2026-07-20: 'all 30+ sessions blue next day when I used ~1/3 — read user submission timestamps, not agent-ai stuff; automation loops may need their own color.'

CORE SEMANTIC (new): split the recency axis into human vs agent.
- lastHumanUsedAt: advanced ONLY by (a) committed envelopes with reasonCode 'user-prompt' (Claude UserPromptSubmit already publishes these — HolyAgentStateBridge.swift:537/551, verified flowing), and (b) genuine focus dwell (1-2s continuous, the anti-launch-sweep rule below) — the dwell path is also the human-use proxy for Codex/OpenCode until those adapters grow a user-submit signal (Codex notify is turn-complete-only today; OpenCode plugin may be able to hook message submission — investigate).
- lastAgentActiveAt: any committed envelope (current lastUsedAt behavior).
- BLUE = lastHumanUsedAt < 24h ago. VIOLET 'on automation' (use existing HolyAgentPalette.workingViolet) = agent active < 24h but NO human use in 24h — watcher loops and long autonomous runs read as automated, never as 'I used this'. Grey 24-48h / sleeping 48h+ key off the LATER of the two axes going quiet. Unread green pip overlays whichever tier dot is true (existing spec below).
- This keying makes the blue axis IMMUNE to the three fake-stamp bugs by construction: launch focus-sweeps, attach-all seeding, and baselines cannot fabricate a user-prompt envelope.

PRIOR DEFECTS (still fix — they poison the seen axis and dwell inputs):
(1) baselineLegacySeenTracking stamps lastUsedAt=now at rollout (HolyModels.swift:206). (2) Attach All seeding marks used via markSeen (HolyModels.swift:284; fallback HolyWorkspaceStore.swift:2293 uses adoption-time createdAt). (3) Launch focus churn transiently satisfies markSessionSeenIfNeeded guards for every session (mn-a0406e, evidence: 22/25 sessions lastSeenAt==lastUsedAt spread across the launch window). Fix: markSeenBaseline(at:) sets lastSeenAt only; seen/used marking requires REAL dwell (1-2s continuous focus) plus a post-restore quiescence window; seenTrackingVersion v2 re-baseline (keep lastSeenAt, reset lastUsedAt to lastAgentFinishedAt ?? nil; lastHumanUsedAt starts nil — honest cold start, sessions earn blue by actual use).

MIGRATION HONESTY: on v2 baseline, day-one roster will show mostly violet/grey rather than blue — that is CORRECT (blue is earned). Rendering: policy recencyKind extraction + unreadBaseKind pip composition per existing spec. Done when: next-day roster shows blue ONLY on sessions Erik actually prompted or genuinely visited in 24h (his ~1/3 test), automation-loop sessions show violet, attach-all/restart changes nothing, full suite green, installed-app verification on both machines.

title: [P0][STATE] Launch-time focus churn marks every session seen+used — all dots blue after every restart
description:
Evidence 2026-07-16: after each app relaunch, persisted attention_metadata shows lastSeenAt == lastUsedAt for 22/25 sessions with timestamps spread across the launch window (18:06–18:13Z for a 18:06Z relaunch). Decode/versioning are NOT the cause (verified: HolyPersistenceCoders symmetric ISO8601; seenTrackingVersion round-trips at v1; persistence reads attention_metadata at HolyWorkspaceDatabasePersistence.swift:159). Mechanism: during window/pane restoration every session's SurfaceView transiently satisfies markSessionSeenIfNeeded's guards (NSApp.isActive + key window + surfaceView.focused, HolyWorkspaceStore.swift:2099) as surfaces initialize, so programmatic focus churn masquerades as the user reading every session. Result: restart erases the entire recency axis — everything reads used-today (blue) for the next 24h.

Fix direction: seen/used marking requires REAL attention, not instantaneous focus — e.g., a dwell requirement (surface focused continuously for 1–2s) and/or a post-restore quiescence window before seen-marking arms. Belongs with mn-596f61's markSeenBaseline/genuine-use split; fix together and verify by relaunching twice and confirming old sessions keep old lastUsedAt.

title: [P2][CORE] Port and benchmark Ghostty renderer-state fairness
description:
Independent hardening finding from the July 17 read-only audit. The original drag complaint occurred outside Holy because of damaged mouse hardware; do not cite it as evidence that this issue caused selection loss.

Evidence:
- Holy core is based on an older Ghostty state and lacks upstream July 9 commit 11b9a6ef1, which adds renderer demand handoff so sustained PTY parsing cannot starve frames on the macOS unfair mutex.
- Holy PTY parsing, renderer snapshots, mouse selection updates, and wheel callbacks contend on renderer_state.mutex.
- A live active-output sample caught renderer frame updates waiting in _os_unfair_lock_lock_slow.
- Upstream documents starvation lasting for the duration of sustained output.

Invariant:
Sustained PTY output must not indefinitely starve renderer or interactive surface work, while terminal throughput and correctness remain intact.

Done when:
- The upstream fairness design is adapted to Holy older Exec loop rather than blindly cherry-picked.
- A repeatable sustained-output benchmark covers parser throughput, renderer frame progress, mouse-selection latency, and scroll latency.
- Renderer and interactive wait times have explicit bounded acceptance thresholds.
- Stress tests cover local and SSH panes across Claude, Codex, OpenCode, and a generic high-output process.
- The installed build passes the benchmark without throughput, deadlock, or rendering regressions.

title: [P1][NOTIFY] Coalesce notification removal and make cleanup idempotent
description:

- Live sampling showed notification and persistence work repeatedly reaching the main thread during rapid session mutations.

Invariant:
Notification state transitions are semantic and idempotent. Re-observing the same state must do no notification-center work, no durable mutation, and no user-visible duplicate or missed alert.

Done when:
- Removal is keyed by stable semantic notification identity and occurs only on a real transition.
- Repeated title, render, focus, roster, restart, and reconnect events produce no redundant removal calls.
- Missed-event replay remains exactly once and notification-click ownership still works.
- Counters expose scheduled, delivered, removed, deduplicated, and replayed operations.
- A 24-hour installed-app soak meets a documented low churn ceiling while passing mn-8179b6 acceptance.

title: [P1][PERF][STATE] Decouple animated terminal titles from session refresh and persistence
description:
Independent finding from the July 17 read-only selection audit. The reported cross-app drag failure was traced to damaged mouse hardware and is NOT a reproduction of this issue.

Evidence:
- Active Codex terminal titles changed about 9-10 times per second; Claude was about 0-1 per second.

- A five-second process sample contained 615 persistence stack samples, including 265 database-save and 151 JSON-encoding samples.

Invariant:
Presentation animation must never become durable session metadata or force whole-roster work. Semantic title and working-directory changes must still propagate reliably for Claude, Codex, OpenCode, and future harnesses.

Done when:
- Spinner-only or frame-only title changes cause zero durable mutations and zero full-roster invalidations.
- Semantic title and cwd changes propagate within a documented bound without being dropped.
- Persistence is coalesced and kept off the interactive drag/render path.
- A busy-Codex installed-app soak measures bounded refresh and persistence rates with no stale titles or lost metadata.
- Regression tests distinguish presentation churn from semantic title changes.

title: [P1][SYNC] Always-on cross-host note/pin sync via tmux user options
description:
Ship the continuous version of the one-time import proven 2026-07-20 (8 notes MacBook→Studio, matched by tmux session name, fill-blank merge, zero conflicts). Erik: 'I want this all the time.'

ARCHITECTURE — the shared tmux server IS the sync bus. No new daemon, no new transport: mirror user-authored metadata as session-scoped user options on the session's OWN tmux server, exactly like @holy_title and @holy_working_directory already do (precedent: title edits ALREADY flow cross-host through this channel — this issue extends the same pattern to notes and Today pins).

Options: @holy_note_v1 (base64-encoded UTF-8; cap 4KB pre-encoding — raw newlines/quotes are unsafe in option values), @holy_note_updated_at_v1 (ms epoch), @holy_today_pin_v1 + @holy_today_pin_updated_at_v1.

WRITE PATH: setNote/setFocus stamp updated_at locally and publish through the existing delivery machinery (HolyTmuxModelLabelUpdateCommand pattern — bounded retry/backoff already built; fail-closed on incomplete tmux identity per house rule). Works identically for local and SSH sessions — the option lands on whichever server hosts the session.

READ PATH: discovery already reads user options (HolyRemoteTmuxDiscoveryService format strings, local + remote); extend to the new options and apply through applyDiscoveredLaunchMetadata.

MERGE SEMANTICS (the contract): remote value wins iff its updated_at is STRICTLY newer than the local edit stamp; an older or timestamp-less remote value never clobbers a local note; local note + absent option → publish local (self-heal + legacy migration on first pass); no flicker loops (applying a remote value must not restamp updated_at). Deletion is a real state: empty-note with newer stamp clears, absent option does not.

NON-GOALS v1: roster order, resume descriptors, sessions that do not share a tmux server, archived rows.

Prior art to read first: today's import script pattern (join key + non-clobber), mn-15ba3d (the eventual full sync contract — this issue is its proven v1 slice), the @holy_title delivery/read path end to end.

IMPLEMENTATION EVIDENCE 2026-07-20 — commit 45772ea65 implements the v1 contract. TDD red→green covered merge ordering, tombstone-vs-absence, byte-exact multiline/emoji base64, field-selective retry coalescing, exact-identity failure, and a real tmux PTY write→option→production-discovery roundtrip (13/13 focused). title: [P1][STATE][CODEX] Working spinner dies mid-turn on long tool-less Codex stretches — lease expires without evidence refresh
description:

- And/or: codex adapter heartbeat if codex exposes any periodic hook/event usable as one.
- Separate but related trap, worth its own check in the doctor: generationVersion bumps regenerate .codex/hooks.json which REQUIRES manual /hooks re-approval per Codex — unapproved sessions silently emit no hook events at all (notify-based finished still flows). Acceptance: a Codex turn reasoning >30min with zero tool calls keeps its spinner for the full turn on the installed app; a killed Codex process drops working within the invalidation window; unapproved-hook sessions show a visible degraded indicator, not fake idle.

title: [P0][RECOVERY] Restore executable discovery: resolve codex/opencode through .zshrc-only PATH entries and bake absolute paths into resume argv
description:
Filed 2026-08-10 from Erik's second-human-contact report (screenshot: codex and opencode rows blocked with "The codex/opencode executable was not found on PATH" while all claude rows restored).

ROOT CAUSE (verified live): HolyRestoreEnvironmentProbe.executableExists (HolyRestoreEngine.swift:966) probes with `/bin/zsh -lc 'command -v <name>'` — a login NON-interactive shell that sources .zprofile but never .zshrc. On this machine codex lives in ~/.nvm/versions/node/v22.16.0/bin (nvm init is .zshrc:30-33) and opencode in ~/.opencode/bin (PATH added in .zshrc); both invisible. claude lives in /opt/homebrew/bin (brew shellenv in .zprofile) — which is exactly why only claude restored. Verified: `zsh -lc 'command -v codex opencode claude'` finds only claude; `zsh -ic` finds all three.

The same login-shell PATH governs the resume command's execution inside the restored tmux session, so fixing the probe alone moves the failure from preflight to launch.

FIX SHAPE (mirrors HolyAgentSessionsResolveClient.wellKnownBinaryPath, HolyRestoreResolveClient.swift:333-346):
- Probe returns an invocable absolute path, not a Bool: login-shell `command -v` stdout first (require a leading /), then a documented well-known-directory walk: ~/.pyenv/shims, ~/.local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin, ~/.opencode/bin, ~/.bun/bin, ~/.volta/bin, and the highest-version ~/.nvm/versions/node/v*/bin containing the executable.
- restoreExact re-resolves at launch time and bakes the absolute path into argv[0] of the resume command (falls back to the bare name only when resolution fails after preflight passed).
- Tests: builder override coverage + engine coverage that a resolved path lands in spec.command.

Done when a codex and an opencode session restore end-to-end on a machine where both binaries are reachable only through .zshrc-initialized PATH entries.

Related debt: this is the third private well-known-path walk (resolver client, this probe; cf. mn-31aaf2's runner unification) — unify later, do not block on it.

Path context (focused repo/board) is already host-local by construction since it derives from the remote session,s discovered cwd. Absent agent-do or ssh failure degrades honestly, naming the host. Suggestion rows for a remote estate spawn their shell ON that host via the automation URL,s existing host/transport params, so the typed command runs where the board lives. Requirement documented: agent-do installed on any host whose sessions you want briefed.
